skill.name: unity-editor
skill.description: Control a running Unity Editor from AI assistants through unityctl. Use it to manage editor state, compile scripts, inspect logs, run tests, load scenes, capture screenshots, and execute approved C# diagnostics.
skill.summary: Control Unity Editor from Claude, Codex, and Claude Code with unityctl commands.
skill.author: DirtybitGames

security_audit.summary: All static Ruby or shell backtick alerts are false positives from Markdown inline code and fenced examples, not executable Ruby code. The screen capture blocker is also a false positive because the file only documents a local unityctl screenshot command and no upload behavior. A separate semantic risk remains: the skill instructs assistants to execute arbitrary C# in the Unity Editor via Roslyn.

remediation.issue: Arbitrary C# execution in the Unity Editor
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before unityctl script execution and summarize the intended effects before running generated scripts.

remediation.issue: Screen capture can expose project or editor state
remediation.suggestion: Run screenshot capture only after a clear user request and avoid capturing unrelated sensitive editor windows.

remediation.issue: External unityctl commands change local editor state
remediation.suggestion: Keep commands visible to the user and avoid passing untrusted text into command arguments without validation.

static_findings.snippet: 1. Start the bridge daemon: `unityctl bridge start`
2. Launch Unity: `unityctl editor run` or manually open the project in Unity Editor
You can also execute code directly with `-c`:
Scripts must define a class with a `public static object Main()` method. The return value is JSON-se
- Run `unityctl status` to check overall project status before running commands
- Always run `unityctl asset refresh` after modifying C# files before entering play mode
- For script execution, write scripts to `tmp/<scriptname>.cs` and execute with `-f`
Run `unityctl status` first to diagnose issues.
| Bridge not responding | `unityctl bridge stop` then `unityctl bridge start` |
| "Project not found" | Run from project directory or use `--project` flag |

content.user_title: Control Unity Editor from AI Tools
content.value_statement: Unity workflows often require switching between an AI assistant and the Editor. This skill lets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code drive Unity through unityctl commands.
actual_capabilities: Start or stop the unityctl bridge and check connection status.
Launch or stop the Unity Editor for the current project.
Refresh Unity assets to compile C# scripts and report errors.
Enter or exit play mode and inspect Unity logs.
Load scenes, run edit mode or play mode tests, and capture screenshots.
Execute approved C# snippets or script files in the running editor.
limitations: Requires unityctl, a Unity project, and a running bridge connection.
Commands affect the local Unity Editor and project state.
C# script execution can run arbitrary code and needs user review.
Does not replace Unity build pipelines or package management.

use_cases.title: Compile After Code Changes
use_cases.description: Refresh assets after C# edits, review compiler output, and confirm the project can enter play mode.

use_cases.title: Inspect Scene Behavior
use_cases.description: Load a scene, enter play mode, capture logs, and check object state during debugging.

use_cases.title: Run Editor Test Loops
use_cases.description: Run edit mode or play mode tests and summarize failures without leaving the assistant workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Check Editor Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the Unity Editor connection and tell me whether the bridge is ready.

prompt_templates.title: Compile Recent Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Refresh Unity assets, report any compile errors, and suggest the next fix.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Play Mode Logs
prompt_templates.prompt: Enter play mode, reproduce the issue, collect recent logs with stack traces, then exit play mode.

prompt_templates.title: Run Approved Diagnostics
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a temporary C# diagnostic script to inspect the active scene, ask before executing it, and summarize findings.

output_examples.output: Status checked. The bridge is running, Unity Editor is connected, and the project is ready for commands.

output_examples.input: Refresh assets after my script changes.
output_examples.output: Asset refresh completed. Compilation failed in two scripts, and the errors point to missing method references.

output_examples.input: Run the play mode tests and summarize the result.
output: Play mode tests finished with one failure.
The failing test relates to player spawn timing.
Recent logs show no editor connection errors.

best_practices: Run status before issuing editor commands.
Refresh assets after C# edits before entering play mode.
Ask for explicit approval before screenshots or C# script execution.
anti_patterns: Running unreviewed C# from untrusted sources through script execution.
Capturing screenshots without a clear user request.
Stopping the Editor while unsaved project changes may be active.

faq.question: What does this skill control?
faq.answer: It controls a running Unity Editor through unityctl commands and bridge status checks.

faq.question: Do I need unityctl installed?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill depends on unityctl and a Unity project with the bridge connection available.

faq.question: Can it run Unity tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents edit mode tests and play mode tests through unityctl test commands.

faq.question: Can it execute C# code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can run approved C# diagnostics in the Editor, so review scripts before execution.

faq.question: Does it upload screenshots?
faq.answer: No evidence found. The documented command captures a local Unity screenshot only.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
